feedback.problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}$ and $f(9)=-10.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=9$ to estimate the value of $f(8.7).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=9$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(9)+{f}^{′}(9)(x-9).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(9)=-10,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}},$ then ${f}^{′}(9)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{9}}=-\frac{2}{3}.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=-10-\frac{2}{3}(x-9).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(8.7)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=8.7.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(8.7) & ≈L(8.7) \\  & =-10-\frac{2}{3}(8.7-9) \\  & =-10-\frac{2}{3}(-0.3) \\  & =-10+0.2 \\  & =-9.8.\end{aligned}
$$
